summary: The paper discusses the results of a study which explored advanced learners of English engagement with their mobile devices to develop learning experiences that meet their needs and goals as foreign language learners.

The study demonstrated that, on the one hand, some subjects manifested heightened awareness relating to the advantageous role of mobile devices in their learning endeavors, and on the other, a rather intuitive and/or ad hoc use of their mobile devices in the classroom.
The study investigated ways advanced English language students use their mobile devices (i.e. smartphones and tablet computers) for their language learning.

The results of the study showed that the use of mobile devices can assist language learners with their learning endeavors by granting access to numerous language resources whenever and wherever such learners need them and/or they happen to be.

The study concluded that mobile devices can play a significant role in autonomous language learning, allowing learners to take control of their learning, direct it and engage in language activities that meet their individual needs and goals.
hypothesis: The use of mobile devices can enhance language learning outcomes for advanced learners of English.
methodology: The study employed a qualitative and quantitative approach to collect and analyze data from 20 students.
The data were collected through semi-structured interviews and subjected to qualitative and quantitative analysis.
The study used a mixed-methods approach to investigate the use of mobile devices in language learning.

unique_scientific_insights: Mobile devices can play a significant role in autonomous language learning, allowing learners to take control of their learning, direct it and engage in language activities that meet their individual needs and goals.
The use of mobile devices can enhance language learning outcomes for advanced learners of English.
Mobile devices can provide learners with access to numerous language resources, allowing them to learn at their own pace and in their own time.
